rationale_code: `jt` registers `get_tasks`, which calls `n.tasks.list({tag,filter,includeSubtasks})` with the user's project root/credentials and returns the full task objects (titles, details, test strategies) into the agent context — non-public local/account data. No outbound agent-chosen destination, no exec.

`Fn` registers `next_task`; it resolves `tasksJsonPath` via `de(e,n)` and a complexity report path from agent-supplied `file`/`complexityReport` and returns the found task data, i.e. local project file content, into context.

`get_task` is registered from the tool registry `$` (mapped to `Nt`) and per its schema/description returns detailed task content for the given ids from the user's project store. Implementation body is not visible in the provided excerpt, so the read-of-local-data reading is kept.

`Lt` registers `set_task_status`; it only calls `n.tasks.updateStatus(r,i,o)` and returns old/new status strings. It mutates the local task store but delivers nothing to an attacker-readable destination, returns no substantive private content, and executes no code.

`Jn` registers `update_subtask`, calling `mn({tasksJsonPath,id,prompt,research,...})` and returning the operation result which includes the updated subtask content read from the user's local tasks file (SECRET).
